sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Precision Steel Injection Molding of Color Snap-Fit Plastic Kits

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; single domestic corporate registry with no separate sub-state registries)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-code-based; commercial companies governed by the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; registration governed by the amended Law of 19 December 2002)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) BITs jointly concluded with over 100 states, including the People's Republic of China, Hong Kong SAR, the Russian Federation, the Republic of Korea, Egypt and Turkey
Luxembourg-United States Income Tax Treaty of 1996 (as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom DTA and exchange-of-information arrangements
EU internal market frameworks: TFEU Articles 49 and 54 (freedom of establishment); EU-Japan EPA facilitating goods market access for anime-figure exports

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended by the Laws of 25 March 2020 and 7 July 2022); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners ('RBE') as amended by the Law of 29 July 2020 and the Law of 8 October 2024 restoring public access; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02; CSSF Circulars 20/744, 21/788 and 24/856; binding measures of the Luxembourg Financial Sanctions Committee.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public (the Law of 8 October 2024 restores public consultation of the RBE: name, nationality, month and year of birth, country of residence, and nature and extent of the beneficial interest are publicly displayed; remaining data fields are accessible only on legitimate-interest request)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / good standing of each direct corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (consular legalization only if the origin state is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each UBO, manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent administrative authority or notary of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification in the country of origin plus Hague Apostille where origin practice requires it, followed by sworn French translation before the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire) of each intended manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the manager's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) together with sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current proof of residential address (utility bill or equivalent issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or municipal authority of the holder's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original or certified true copy; apostille required only for high-risk source countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / financial standing letter covering the source of the initial share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution holding the subscriber's funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Client-authenticated signature of the issuing bank (no apostille) - accepted by Luxembourg notaries and banks for standard-risk manufacturing clients

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP enhanced due diligence under Article 5 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004; mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and counterparties against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the US OFAC SDN list, the UK OFSI list and the Luxembourg Financial Sanctions Committee list; continuous transaction monitoring; 5-year retention of due diligence records; CSSF-supervised AML/CFT training and a risk-based compliance program.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), https://www.lbr.lu; the pre-incorporation name check and reservation must be lodged electronically via an authorized professional (notary or registered filing agent).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in the RCS in French (or in German/Luxembourgish where the constituting documents use that form); non-Latin script marks (e.g., Japanese romaji for 'MECHA' or Chinese pinyin) require a concurrent French transliteration or official translation; the legal-form suffix 'S.A.R.L.' / 'S.à r.l.' is mandatory.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: LUXEMBOURG (authorization required as a State- or public-sector-linked token)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reserved name lapses automatically if the notarial deed and the RCS/RESA filings are not completed within 30 days; a fresh availability check is required for any re-filing. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) submit a revised name via the LBR e-platform (previously paid fees are not refunded), or (ii) within one month of the refusal, appeal to the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg in summary proceedings (référé) under Article 7 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002; a judicial order favorable to the applicant is executed by the RCS registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory seat: the SARL must maintain a 'siège statutaire' at a real physical address in Luxembourg capable of receiving service of process. A commercial domiciliation solution is available under the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation, subject to an authorized domiciliation agent and genuine administrative presence. As ISIC 3240 requires a physical injection-molding production facility, Luxembourg substance will consist of management, sales administration and finance; the foreign production site must be supported by a transfer-pricing file and a VAT registration analysis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: unannounced inspections by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) occur mainly on VAT, payroll and substance indicators; estimated annual likelihood of an on-site visit within the first three years is approximately 8-12% for a low-risk, standard manufacturing entity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation of the SARL (drafting, reading and authentication of the articles of association)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (statutory tariff law of 10 July 2020 and applicable Grand-Ducal regulation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff; prevailing market benchmark of EUR 1,000-1,450 per standard SARL deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration formalities (dossier de dépôt) through the Luxembourg Business Registers e-platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of EUR 19 per Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 December 2016

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of EUR 19.50 per publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO identification, corporate documentation and coordination by Luxembourg counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard SARL incorporation package including AML/CFT KYC review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners) initial filing and subsequent consistency check
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RBE register via LBR; fees absorbed in the notarial package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee (free mandatory registration)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilles, notarial certifications and sworn French translations of origin-country documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authorities (apostille) and Luxembourg sworn translators (traducteurs assermentés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of EUR 8-12 per translated page; origin-country apostille fees estimated at USD 150-250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation blocked account (compte bloqué) setup and bank due diligence for deposit of the EUR 12,000 minimum share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 300 for onboarding a standard-risk manufacturing client

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office / domiciliation and administrative substance services (pro-rated first quarter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized Luxembourg domiciliation or corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 250-350 per month for domiciliation, mail handling and statutory agent services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 710-1 to 710-23 (SARL regime); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and Annual Accounts (RCS Law); Law of 2 September 2011 on the Freedom of Establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif / statuts) executed before a Luxembourg notary, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid-up in cash and/or in kind before incorporation; cash capital must be deposited on a blocked account of a Luxembourg credit institution and evidenced by a bank blocking certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds) produced to the notary; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation report where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The subscribers, having resolved to form a Luxembourg Société à Responsabilité Limitée named [LUX SARL], hereby RESOLVE: (1) to ratify the execution of the notarial articles of association signed this day; (2) to acknowledge the fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 evidenced by the bank blocking certificate; (3) to adopt the registered office at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (4) to appoint [Name] as manager (gérant) with full powers of administration and representation; (5) to direct the manager to complete all RCS registrations, RESA publication, tax and social security filings; and (6) to apply for all industrial, environmental and establishment licenses required for the manufacture of snap-fit mecha model kits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal (ejustice.lu / rcs.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed corporate name 'LUX SARL' to verify conformity and availability. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must comply with Luxembourg public order rules. Obtain the official name reservation confirmation before proceeding to notarization.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation form
Identity documents of all shareholders
Draft articles of association indicating proposed corporate name and duration
Power of attorney if filed through a professional agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, promptly submit an amended reservation with a revised distinctive name; an adverse decision may be appealed before the administrative courts within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Issuance of Blocking Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation, deposit the full minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 (plus incorporation expenses), and obtain the attestation de blocage de fonds from the bank. The certificate must be addressed to the Luxembourg notary and must evidence that the capital is irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the company to be formed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Shareholders' identification documents and beneficial owner declarations
Source of funds documentation (bank KYC/AML file)
Brief business plan and intended activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/KYC queries, supplement documentation as requested; if the blocking certificate contains errors, the bank will re-issue a corrected version at no additional statutory cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association in a notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary. The deed must be drafted in French or German and must contain the corporate form, name, registered office, corporate object (manufacture of snap-fit mecha model kits), duration, share capital, shareholder details, and powers of the manager. The notary verifies legality, capital deposit, and the legal capacity of the subscribers, and files the required criminal record and bankruptcy declarations.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking certificate
Draft articles of association
Shareholders' passports and proof of residential address
Beneficial owner declaration under the Law of 13 January 2019
Notarized powers of attorney if a shareholder is not personally present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary may require rectification of unlawful or void clauses; the deed is re-drafted and re-executed at the notary's office before any RCS filing may proceed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Registration Office, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and the incorporation dossier electronically through the RCS e-filing portal. Pay the statutory filing fee of EUR 19. The RCS verifies the legality of the deed, assigns the RCS registration number, and enters the company in the register. Legal personality of the SARL is acquired as of the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Bank blocking certificate
Statement of compliance of managers/shareholders (criminal record)
Power of attorney to the filing agent
RCS electronic filing form (carte RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, the notary or company counsel must submit a written response with curative amendments within 15 days; any refusal may be contested before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) seized in commercial matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically transmits the deed and statutory particulars to RESA for mandatory publication. Publication is free of charge and is a condition for the opposability of the incorporation to third parties; the entity receives a RESA publication reference.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (generated automatically)
Notarial deed transmitted automatically by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, file a correction request with the RCS; note that until publication, the deed is not effective against third parties, so prompt verification is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security and Establishment-Permit Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED); Ministry of the Economy – Guichet unique for the autorisation d'établissement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the CCSS for social security; file the declaration of commencement of activity with the ACD for corporate income tax; apply to the AED for a Luxembourg VAT number; submit the application for the autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011, demonstrating professional qualification and sound financial standing for the industrial manufacturing activity.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the notarial deed
Manager's identity document and professional qualification certificates
Lease agreement or title for the registered office and industrial premises
Site plan and description of the injection-moulding production equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is refused, the applicant may request re-examination by the Ministry of the Economy within the statutory period and thereafter appeal to the Administrative Tribunal; incomplete tax/social filings may be cured by submitting the missing declarations through the respective online portals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate-General for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, Commission d'établissement / Guichet unique des autorisations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on the Freedom of Establishment, required for the industrial manufacture of snap-fit model kits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Administration) of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Class 4 'commodo-incommodo' prior declaration (déclaration) for small-capacity plastics injection-moulding operations; reclassified to Class 3 (operating authorization) if installed polymer-processing capacity exceeds the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 1999; a full EIA (étude d'impact) under the amended Law of 22 May 2008 (as amended by the Law of 15 May 2018) is not mandatory for small-scale toy/model-kit manufacturing unless Annex II thresholds on production capacity or site sensitivity are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the Grand-Ducal Regulation limits for industrial effluents into public sewers (COD, suspended solids, heavy metals); volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from injection moulding must comply with Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) and the applicable EU VOC emission limit values; plastic waste is subject to mandatory separate collection, traceability and recycling reporting under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on Waste Management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the municipal fire authority and the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); structural load inspection certificates for injection-moulding machinery must be issued by an approved engineering bureau; workplace occupational clearance and machinery conformity verification are performed by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including the mandatory risk assessment and safety measures prescribed by the amended Law of 17 June 1994 on Occupational Health and Safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portals: myguichet.lu, guichet.lu, and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first file for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through myguichet.lu via a Luxembourg professional appointed as authorized signatory or incorporation agent. After RCS registration, the entity automatically receives a business identification number (matricule d'identification). The entity must then submit a separate VAT registration application to the AEDT (form 640 or via myguichet.lu) indicating its intended taxable activities in Luxembourg. For a SARL, the RCS extract, articles of association, proof of registered office, identity documents of managers, and a signed declaration confirming the commencement of taxable activities are required. The TIN (matricule) is used for corporate income tax; the VAT number (numéro de TVA) is issued separately by the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law does not provide a check-the-box election comparable to the US. A SARL is, by default, a separately assessable corporate taxpayer. Optional regimes available include the election for joint filing under the Luxembourg integrated fiscal regime (intégration fiscale), VAT grouping election, and the shipping or IP box regimes where eligibility is satisfied. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD and Luxembourg domestic anti-hybrid provisions may restrict elective outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic registration threshold applies to a Luxembourg-established taxable person; any person carrying out taxable transactions is required to register for VAT irrespective of turnover level. For cross-border distance sales of goods into Luxembourg by non-established suppliers, the EU distance selling threshold is currently EUR 10,000 per year, measured against overall distance sales within the EU.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control for all B2B/B2C invoicing. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for public sector supplies (B2G) using the PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format, and e-invoicing is accepted generally with certain authentication requirements. No digital stamping or API-based real-time reporting to the tax administration is imposed as of the current reporting date, though invoice storage and access obligations align with EU VAT invoicing rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, provided the goods leave the EU. Services that are directly linked to the export of goods or supplied to non-EU customers where the place of supply is outside the EU also qualify for zero-rating. The supplier must hold documentary evidence establishing that the goods have been physically exported, the export transaction is commercial in substance, and the recipient is established abroad. For an action figure manufacturing scope, typical qualifying exports include goods sold to non-EU distributors or customers with import customs documentation proving entry into a third country.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation / Single Administrative Document SAD)
Proof of leaving the EU (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR road consignment note, or railway consignment note)
Commercial invoice issued by the Luxembourg SARL
Payment proof (SWIFT wire or PayPal transaction record)
For certain countries, a certificate of arrival or customs import documentation issued by the destination customs office
Internal transport records and proof of dispatch from Luxembourg warehouse
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incorrect or fraudulent zero-rating claims may trigger recharacterization as taxable domestic supplies, resulting in VAT assessment at 16%, plus default interest and late-payment penalties up to 10% per annum. Intentional or repeated irregularity attracts administrative fines ranging from EUR 750 to EUR 12,500, or up to double the evaded tax, and criminal sanctions for tax fraud may be imposed. The AEDT may also claw back input VAT correspondingly, deny refunds for up to five years, and impose a 10% penalty for gross negligence or intentionally documented fraud. Directors and managing officers of the SARL may incur joint and several liability for unjustified VAT benefits when they knew or should have known of the abuse.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem, with prudential regulation and AML/CFT supervision delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); no separate foreign exchange administration exists in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc was permanently replaced by the euro (EUR) on 1 January 1999; the SARL operates under a fully liberalised regime. Both current-account and capital-account operations are unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Directive 88/361/EEC. Profit repatriation and dividend distributions require only ordinary corporate formalities under the law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (annual shareholders' meeting, distributable-reserve sufficiency, and certain minimum statutory reserve requirements). Dividend withholding tax of 15% applies at a standard domestic rate, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months, or to treaty-reduced rates for third-country investors. No prior exchange-control approval, central-bank notification, or convertibility permit is required for any inward or outward payment; the only residual obligation is periodic balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export receipts. A Luxembourg SARL may freely retain foreign currency (USD, JPY, CNY) in multi-currency accounts, convert into EUR at market rates, or use the proceeds to settle external trade payables. Non-financial corporations are subject exclusively to BCL statistical reporting rules: direct investment flows and positions vis-à-vis non-residents must be reported on a quarterly basis when the accumulated transaction threshold exceeds EUR 12.5 million per reporting period; below this threshold, the intermediating credit institution reports on the company's behalf.
key_regulatory_instruments: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law)
CSSF Regulation 20-05 on central administration, internal governance and risk management
CSSF Circular 18/698 on AML/CFT procedures and customer due diligence
EU Regulation 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds
EU Regulation 184/2005 on community statistics concerning balance of payments
EU Regulation 2018/1672 on controls on cash entering or leaving the Union
Law of 25 March 2020 (permanent legislative framework) permitting remote video customer identification

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account, Trade Finance Account (LCs, guarantees), Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and FX/Treasury Line (forwards, FX swaps)
Operational Account and Cross-Border Settlement Account
Operational Account and Documentary Credit Facility
Wealth and Treasury Account (asset-heavy treasury structures only)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for ancillary operational flows; Low as a primary treasury rail. An EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution or Payment Institution (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Qonto, or N26 Business) may lawfully provide the SARL with a working-capital account, EUR/GBP/USD receivables collection, and expedited supplier payout via IBAN and SWIFT connectivity under PSD2 passporting. However, such EMIs do not hold the legal status of a credit institution in Luxembourg, are not CSSF-supervised as banks, cannot open a broad documentary-credit line or issuance of standby LCs, and are generally unsuitable for large inbound capital escrow or trade-finance disbursements. The SARL must retain at least one Tier-1 CSSF-regulated bank as the core treasury counterparty; EMIs are permitted only as a payment-rail supplement, with a maximum balance per EMI capped at operational float requirements (recommended EUR 50,000 - 100,000). PayPal serves the low-risk DTC/anime-hobbyist direct-sales channel under the target payment rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permissible under Luxembourg law but is practically constrained. The Law of 25 March 2020, integrating video-identification provisions into the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, permits a credit institution to onboard corporate clients via video conference where the natural-person representative presents a valid identity document, liveness detection is performed, and certified document copies are subsequently delivered by post or via a secure electronic sharing platform. Nevertheless, most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require, for a foreign-managed SARL: (a) at least one ultimate beneficial owner or authorised manager to attend a physical due-diligence meeting at the bank's Luxembourg head office or at a CSSF-recognised correspondent branch (for BCEE, BIL and ING, the physical meeting mandate is near-universal for non-EU residents); (b) a notarised power of attorney appointing a local professional (Luxembourg resident) as authorised signatory if no director is domiciled in Luxembourg; or (c) delivery of an original bank reference, recent audited financial statements, and apostilled passport copies. Practical mandate: physical attendance of the statutory manager (gérant) or of a formally appointed local agent is strongly recommended; fully remote onboarding is feasible only when the bank's approved e-KYC provider (e.g., onfido / Veriff style service integrated by the bank) is accepted, which remains bank-specific and discretionary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner (BO) tax resident in a FATF grey-listed or high-risk third country, or a PEP (politically exposed person) with unexplained wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract, BO tax-residence certificate, Lex/Deloitte/PwC corporate-structure chart, CV and source-of-wealth statement, notarised asset-declaration affidavits, and a detailed business-purpose letter demonstrating the commercial logic of the manufacturing SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border trade velocity to/from jurisdictions with elevated trade-based money-laundering indices, particularly steel-mold tooling purchases from non-OECD partners or plastic-resin sourcing from sanctioned petrochemical producers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed supply-chain contracts with counterparty KYB packages (registered address, trade licence, bank confirmation), customs declarations (EU Single Administrative Document), bills of lading, third-party inspection certificates (SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek), insurance certificates, and a sanctions-screening policy evidencing Denied-Party List checks on all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected transaction turnover disproportionate to the SARL's declared share capital (minimum EUR 12,500 for a standard SARL; recommended EUR 50,000+ actual capital) or high cash-flow intensity inconsistent with a manufacturing balance sheet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12- to 24-month audited cash-flow projections, management accounts, purchase orders from end-distributors (e.g., anime-specialty retail chains, licensing agents), sales contracts, royalty/licensing agreements, inventory tooling invoices, freight-forwarder service agreements, and a written explanation of working-capital cyclicality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party capital injection without clear corporate purpose, e.g., shareholder loans, convertible notes, or family advances made via foreign banks outside the EU.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised loan agreements with market-rate interest terms, subordination letters to external creditors, cash-pooling agreements, sworn declaration of source of funds, bank statements of the lending shareholder covering at least 6 months, and, if applicable, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance's registration of the loan for BCL statistical purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Involvement of offshore-licensed or opaque intermediate entities in the ownership chain (e.g., a Cyprus, Delaware, or BVI topco with no substance).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purpose-of-entity memorandum, substance documentation (employees, premises, payroll) of the intermediate entity, consolidated group annual report, tax transparency certificates (e.g., EU tax-residency certificate and, where applicable, a valid economic-substance filing), and an organigramme approved by a Luxembourg notary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for equity subscription: (1) the shareholder wires funds from its home bank via SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's EUR account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank; (2) the payment must be tagged with the BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct-investment equity ('Equity capital excluding reinvestment of earnings') and must include the SARL's registered legal name and RCS number (e.g., LU-XXXXXX) in the beneficiary field; (3) the originator must provide complete originator information (legal name, address, account number) pursuant to EU Regulation 2015/847, otherwise the receiving bank must reject or hold the funds; (4) the receiving bank will require a board/shareholder resolution, the updated coordinate list of authorised signatories, a completed source-of-funds questionnaire for amounts exceeding EUR 100,000, and the notarised deed of contribution if the capital increase is registered with the RCS; (5) upon confirmation of receipt, the SARL must update the RBE register and file an annual accounts note in the Luxembourg trade registry; (6) if the cumulative direct-investment flow exceeds EUR 12.5 million in a single quarter, the SARL must file a direct BCL balance-of-payments report online via the BCL's e-reporting portal; below the threshold the bank reports on its behalf. For convertible notes, the routing is identical but requires a tax-law validation that the note qualifies as a genuine debt instrument and not as re-characterised equity for Luxembourg corporate income and net-wealth tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails used: (a) Packaging/moulding materials sourced from EU suppliers (plastic resin pellets, pigments, packaging) - settle via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant within the EU, typically clearing through TARGET2 within the same business day; (b) high-precision steel injection moulds and tooling from non-EU toolmakers (China, Taiwan, Japan) - settle via irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit at sight (MT700/MT710 commercial LC) advised by the Luxembourg bank through the beneficiary's confirming bank, or via SWIFT MT103 direct wire with a signed commercial invoice, packing list, and bills of lading as underlying evidence; (c) royalty and licensing payments to anime/IP licensors in Japan or the US - SWIFT MT103 quoting the relevant tax-treaty withholding position (Luxembourg-Japan income tax treaty or Luxembourg-US treaty) and accompanied by the licensor's W-8BEN-E/Tax board form and the royalty invoice; (d) freight, customs brokerage, and third-party logistics - SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT, with supplier invoices matched to the shipping manifest; (e) PayPal-based DTC micro-trades in the sub-EUR 10,000 tranche - PayPal mass-payout or instant-transfer bridge to the SARL's associated operational bank account; PayPal proceeds are swept daily to the primary bank to minimise whale-high fees and FX margin. For all outbound non-EUR disbursements, the bank's instructions should include the SWIFT BIC, IBAN/CLABE/ABA equivalent, and the correspondent-bank routing confirmed in advance by the receiving bank to avoid MT202 cover rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD plain-vanilla outright forward contracts (tenor 1-24 months) executed under an ISDA Master Agreement or the bank's standard FX Master Confirmation Agreement; collateral is generally not required below a EUR 2 million notional.
EUR/JPY outright forwards for royalty and tooling payments to Japanese counterparties, locked in conjunction with daily LIBOR/EURIBOR (BOFR) conversion conventions.
EUR/CNY deliverable forwards (where the Luxembourg bank has CNY clearing capability via Hong Kong) or non-deliverable forwards (CNH NDF) for Chinese tooling suppliers holding offshore CNY accounts.
FX swaps (swap-out/swap-in) for temporary EUR liquidity mobilisation against USD trade receivables.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS) only for large cap-ex financing linked to an underlying EC-laundered loan; must be cleared or exchanged via a registered EU trade repository (e.g., REGIS-TR or DTCC Data Repository) according to EMIR Refit reporting obligations.
Vanilla European-style FX options on EUR/USD for downside protection on major export orders; premium payment must be considered as a taxable treasury expense.

Non-deliverable swaps on exotic currencies (e.g., EUR/BRL, EUR/TRY) are permissible if the bank maintains an approved NDF settlement policy and the notional is supported by an underlying overdue trade payable; the CRD V/EMIR risk-floor applies.

PayPal currency conversion is contractually available but is classified as a non-bank treasury hedging mechanism; it is permissible only for immaterial DTC transaction balances and does not satisfy prudent FX-hedging policy requirements.
treasury_policy_notes: The SARL's treasury policy must centralise all FX exposure in EUR reporting currency; all significant non-EUR revenues (USD, JPY) should be hedged on a rolling 50-70% forward basis with a tenor aligned to the average trade-receivable cycle.

All outbound payments exceeding EUR 50,000 must be released via dual-signature authorisation (at least two of: gérant, deputy director, finance controller) through the bank's online business portal, with an automated anti-duplication check.
Mould tooling capital expenditure in China should be routed using documentary-only collection (D/P) for low-risk repetitions and irrevocable LC at sight for first-transaction counterparties.
Monthly reconciliation must be performed between SWIFT MT940/MT950 statements, PayPal reports, and the SAP-derived cash ledger to detect any wash-back or virtual-currency conversion blockage.

For intraday liquidity, the SARL should maintain a same-day EUR credit line (backstop) with its primary bank equivalent to one monthly fixed-cost cycle (approximately EUR 500,000) to bridge timing mismatches on large outbound trade settlements.

All hedging instruments must be executed only with CSSF-licensed or passported EEA counterparties; any non-EEA hedge provider requires prior internal treasury policy approval and a CSSF-authorised credit assessment.

All cash pooling structures (if introduced later with group entities) must respect the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF circular 12/552 on intragroup netting, with an analytically documented arm's-length guarantee fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholders' approval and in any event no later than seven months after the financial year-end; calendar-year SARL: by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing triggers a formal notice from the RCS, potential criminal fine for the legal representatives, court-ordered filing, and after repeated default (generally three years without accounts) administrative dissolution and deletion from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the first anniversary of the initial RBE registration and annually thereafter; no-change confirmation remains mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm, or confirmation containing materially inaccurate data, constitutes an AML/CFT compliance offence carrying criminal fines and possible administrative sanctions; continuing non-compliance may flag the entity as non-compliant and restrict access to certain corporate acts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City rate (CIT 17% on taxable income above EUR 175,000; 15% on the first EUR 175,000; 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT; 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption of qualifying IP-derived net income, effective rate approximately 5.04%; 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period); EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive zero-WHT implementation; investment tax credit for SMEs; super-deduction for digital and ecological transition investments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), filed electronically via the ACD e-filing portal (MyGuichet.lu / impotsdirects.public.lu)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline: 31 March of the year following the tax year (Art. 160 AO); ACD administrative extension to 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; assessment tax payable within one month of the notice (bulletin de taxation)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS number, 13-digit matricule fiscal, legal form (SARL), registered office, principal ISIC 3240 activity, directors and authorized signatories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SARL files as domestic taxpayer; non-resident shareholders are not listed on Form 470; identify foreign directors or managers only if they hold signatory authority

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period covered by the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact civil-law financial year of the SARL; first return may cover a shortened period not exceeding 12 months

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss per the statutory annual accounts filed with the RCS Luxembourg
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile with the audited or approved financial statements; attach the balance sheet and profit-and-loss account as annexes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to be added back: fines, excess remuneration, non-wholly and exclusively incurred costs, 50% of certain financing and entertainment expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reject any expense not supported by contracts, invoices, or bank evidence traceable to the SARL's toy-manufacturing business

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income and deductions: participation-exempt dividends, IP box income (80% exemption), tax-exempt subsidies, and prior-year loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate the underlying participation, IP ownership, and 12-month holding period; beneficial ownership must be demonstrated for all exempt flows

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable base after add-backs, deductions, and loss utilization; the basis for the 17%/15% CIT progression
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the base is computed in EUR and reconciles to the annual accounts; any adjustment must be documented in the return annexes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of tax loss carryforward: year of origin, amount utilized, remaining balance; maximum 17-year carryforward for losses incurred from FY2017
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a permanent register of loss carryforwards; anti-abuse rules may forfeit losses upon change of control if the business activity is substantially altered

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of all direct and indirect participations, holding percentages, acquisition cost, and holding period, used to claim the participation exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide acquisition agreements, transfer documents, and proof that the distributee is subject to an equivalent corporate income tax for post-2021 distributions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of intra-group transactions: cross-border royalties for IP licensing, intercompany loans, and sales of mecha model kits; the arm's length principle applies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that Master File and Local File thresholds are assessed; documentation must be available within 60 days of an ACD request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ATAD 2 disclosure of any hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities, or deductible-payment mismatches involving non-EU jurisdictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to notify carries an administrative fine up to EUR 250,000; scrutinize any flow to low-tax or hybrid-transparent entities

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the return is complete and accurate, signed by a director or authorized representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: False certification triggers the criminal fraud provisions of Art. 396 AO; electronic signature on the portal is binding

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: written reminder followed by administrative penalty of EUR 100 to EUR 1,000 (Art. 162 AO); official estimated assessment with a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax; late payment interest of 0.6% per month (fraction of a month counted) until full settlement; deliberate non-filing may escalate to criminal tax fraud proceedings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (Art. 147 LIR); full exemption applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the domestic participation-exemption protocol for qualifying shareholders holding at least 10% (or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost) for an uninterrupted 12-month period
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder files a withholding tax refund or reduced-rate application with the ACD, submitting the official certificate of tax residence (attestation de résidence fiscale / Form 100) from the home tax authority, accompanied by ownership and holding-period evidence; claims generally must be submitted within the statutory limitation period ending 31 December of the third year following the distribution year; beneficial ownership and economic substance in Luxembourg must be demonstrable to defeat GAAR challenges
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties: 0% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax (no general WHT on outbound interest or royalties); EU Interest and Royalties Directive implemented; payments to non-qualifying hybrid or low-tax jurisdictions may be recharacterized under the anti-abuse regime, and late-interest or notional royalty adjustments can be made under the arm's length rules

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File mandatory when group net turnover exceeds EUR 50 million and intra-group transactions exceed EUR 100,000; simplified Local File for lower-value flows; Country-by-Country Report required when consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750 million; documentation must be produced within 60 days of an ACD request
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg enforces substance requirements through the domestic general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit), the ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 implementations, beneficial-ownership precedent for treaty and Directive relief, and ACD circular practice; the SARL must maintain in Luxembourg its registered office, administrative employees, board decision-making, operational bank accounts, and transfer pricing records; the participation exemption and IP box are denied where the entity lacks genuine economic activity and is used as a conduit for the mecha model kit IP or royalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of income from SWIFT-wire and PayPal sales channels, fabrication of invoices, concealment of beneficial ownership, or overstatement of deductible expenses in Form 470
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (Art. 396 AO): imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and/or a fine up to EUR 25,000; aggravated fraud (Art. 397 AO): fine up to EUR 250,000; plus full tax reassessment, 0.6% monthly late interest, and an official-assessment surcharge up to 10%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are prosecuted personally; courts may order civil restitution of evaded taxes, freeze personal and corporate assets, impose travel bans, and disqualify directors from managing commercial companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letterbox SARL without premises, employees, or operational substance, established solely to channel dividends, interest, or royalties from the action-figure/mecha model-kit IP through Luxembourg to a low-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization of the structure; denial of participation-exemption dividend treatment and treaty withholding tax relief; administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 for hybrid-mismatch notification failures (Art. 168quater LIR); reclassification of the Luxembourg entity as a foreign principal's permanent establishment with retroactive assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability for the abusive arrangement, claw-back claims by creditors and tax authority in insolvency, and criminal prosecution in cases of deliberate sham; travel bans and management prohibitions may be imposed in criminal proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL to layer third-party funds via SWIFT/PayPal payment rails inconsistent with legitimate high-precision plastic-kit manufacturing; undisclosed indirect beneficial ownership; suspicious cash deposits without statutory AML reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02: supervisory fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; Penal Code Art. 506-1 money laundering: imprisonment from 5 to 10 years and fine from EUR 12,500 to EUR 1,250,000, doubled to EUR 5,000,000 in organized-crime circumstances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable as AML gatekeepers; sanctions include preventive asset freezing, international travel bans, professional bans, personal fines, and imprisonment upon conviction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for IP royalties, model-kit exports, or financing outside the arm's length range, or failing to produce Master File/Local File documentation within 60 days of an ACD audit request
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax audit adjustment of the Luxembourg taxable base with 0.6% monthly late interest; administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 for documentation and disclosure failures; double taxation exposure without mutual agreement procedure relief in severe cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct mispricing or destroy evidence are jointly liable for the tax undercharge; aggravated conduct may be prosecuted as tax fraud under Art. 396 AO, triggering imprisonment and personal fines
